title: Still True in Daylight
description:
At 3 AM it felt right.

In the office during the day, in front of the manager, eating alone at lunch — does that conviction hold?

Time to check.

choices.text: Yes. I think the same thing in daylight.
choices.result_text:
The midnight resolve was still there in the afternoon sun.

That mattered. Not just brave in the dark — the same person when it's bright.

choices.text: Honestly, there are moments when it wavers.
choices.result_text:
He admitted it. The weight of the daytime sometimes diluted the 3 AM conviction.

But recognizing it was itself the effort not to waver. You can't hold what you can't see.

title: Checking the 43-Year-Old Vision
description:
He pulled out the old notebook in a corner cafe. The version of himself at 43.

He reread what he'd written back then. Is the current him heading that direction?

An honest comparison.

choices.text: Direction's right. Just a matter of speed.
choices.result_text:
If the direction is right, speed can be adjusted.

One sentence he'd written then caught his eye again. The Minjun of today could have written it. That was enough of a midpoint check.

choices.text: The direction has shifted. Time to revise.
choices.result_text:
He revised it. A vision isn't fixed.

The 43 he imagined then and the 43 he imagines now are different. More concrete. More honest. Strangely, more real.

title: Does the Standard Still Hold
description:
He'd decided: Gangnam is a benchmark. Wherever he can live at that level is fine.

Now, from a gosiwon room — or a small studio — he should check whether that conviction is still standing.

Is it still true?

choices.text: Still true. I'm the standard, not the address.
choices.result_text:
The small room made that thought sharper.

The standard doesn't start when he moves to Gangnam. It starts now, here, in how he spends this day. That's already the beginning.

choices.text: Honestly, I do want the address itself sometimes.
choices.result_text:
Desire being specific isn't a problem.

Whether benchmark or destination, the direction is the same. Language matters less than movement.
